items.title: Harry Fairconnetue Interview, 1962-11-11
items.q: Eddie Thomas playing drums. That's my old drummer where I first started.

ctx.x: So, 8 and 29, okay. 8 or 9 and 29. It'll be about 38, maybe, something like that. Could have been about that. Yeah, yeah, well, you can figure those things out from those landmarks, you know, like that. Oh, yeah. Everybody has landmarks in their life. That's right. Uh, well, let's see. Those early bands before Desdune, who was in some of them that you played with? Even non-professional jobs when you just played for fun, maybe.

All right. Oscar Collins, Paul Maurice, Johnny Tonequale, Eddie Thomas, Ogie Socia, and, um... What about Eddie Thomas the drummer? Yeah, Eddie Thomas the drummer and Giger, Anderson Edward, the bass player. Well, what was Ogie's playing at that time? Oh, I got, I got, I got that messed up too. Because Oscar Collins was the trombone playing, both of them couldn't be in the same band. Later, I played with Ogie. Oscar Collins was the trombone playing this band, you see. And Maurice? And Maurice. What did he play?…
I don't even get that. Collins was the leader? No, Paul Maurice was the leader.

items.title: Harry Fairconnetue Interview, 1962-11-11
items.q: The interviewee mentions 'Eddie guy' only in the context of the interviewer asking if 'Guys' (likely a mishearing of Eddie Guy or a different person) could find jobs, and the interviewee responds with uncertainty ('I don't know. I think he did though.') without describing a personal or professional

ctx.x: Yeah. You was a leader and he was a manager or what? I didn't work. I was a leader, manager, and everything.

Yeah. At that time. You had your own bass. Yeah. And then I had my brother-in-law playing guitar with me. Eddie Palu, that's the same name. Eddie Thomas playing drums. That's my old drummer where I first started. And Harold. Harold. That was my main man, yeah. And you lived over here? No. I used to stay on vacation time and on weekends, you know. Then I wouldn't come over here on weekends when they'd send for me. I'd send for him. I'd send for him. And that guy, I mean, associate used to send for Clayton a lot of…
Well, how did you work that then? You mostly had jobs on the weekend when you lived here.
